summary: Mouse hears a HELICOPTER and goes to the draped windows; his CELLULAR RINGS and he answers it. TANK warns him over the phone that 'TANK warns him over the phone that the hardline is severed, it's a trap, and he needs to get out. Mouse yanks open the curtain., says 'Oh no,' and discovers the windows are bricked up. As the RUMBLE of combat BOOTS BUILDS, they explode into the room, trapping Mouse.

what_changes.before: Unaware he is in a trap, merely reacting to the helicopter noise.
what_changes.after: Learns from Tank that the hardline was cut and it is a trap, so he must get out.
what_changes.evidence: They cut the hardline!  It's a trap

what_changes.before: Potentially able to escape through the windows.
what_changes.after: Trapped; the windows are bricked up and combat boots explode into the room.
what_changes.evidence: The windows are bricked up.  Mouse spins

event_hint.one_line: Enemy forces close in and burst into Room 1313, trapping Mouse inside.

uncertain: Whether Mouse survives the raid or how he escapes.
Exactly who the combat BOOT-wearing intruders are.

minds.wants: To understand the noise that's pulling him to the window and, once Tank's warning lands, to get out of the room before the trap closes.
minds.feels: A fast, compounding dread — the helicopter is already wrong, Tank's voice confirms it, and the bricked-up window converts confusion into the specific terror of being sealed in. There is no time to think, only to react.
minds.shows: Only the reflexive, almost childish 'Oh no' — a small, stunned sound that betrays he has already grasped the whole shape of the trap before his body catches up. He spins, physically cornered, as the boots arrive.
minds.basis: He moves to the windows on the helicopter sound before the phone even rings, so he's already on edge; Tank's V.O. 'It's a trap! Get out!' is what he receives; his 'Oh no' on seeing the bricked-up windows and his spin as combat boots explode in are the only things he gets to express. The scene gives him no speech beyond that one involuntary line.

believes_about.belief: That Tank is still reachable and warning him from somewhere safe, so there is a chance to get out if he moves fast.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank is right that it's a trap, but Mouse's belief that escape is still possible is wrong — the windows are already bricked up, so the exit Tank assumes exists is gone.

believes_about.belief: That the room's physical layout is stable and reliable, as it always has been — windows are windows.
believes_about.wrong_because: In the Matrix the environment is editable, and the Agents have just rewritten the wall (foreshadowed by the cable being cut in sc-096 and the bricking described in ev-022); Mouse's assumption that reality here is fixed is exactly what kills him.

minds.wants: To get the warning to Mouse fast enough that Mouse gets out before the room is sealed.
minds.feels: The adrenaline of having just recognised the trap (sc-094 'It's a trap!') and now racing against a closing window, speaking in clipped imperatives because there is no breath for explanation.
minds.shows: Nothing visible — he is only a voice on the line, and what reaches this scene is three staccato commands: 'The hardline's been severed! It's a trap! Get out!'
minds.basis: In sc-094 Tank is the one who 'sees what was changed' and declares the trap; sc-096 shows the hardline being cut, which is exactly what Tank reports here. His dialogue is pure imperative with no greeting or elaboration, consistent with someone transmitting under time pressure.

believes_about.belief: That Mouse can still escape if he acts immediately — that the warning arrives in time and an exit remains open.
believes_about.wrong_because: By the time Tank's call connects, the windows are already bricked up (the Matrix has been rewritten), so Tank's assumption that Mouse can simply 'get out' is already false.

minds.wants: To close the room and take whoever is inside — to complete the trap.
minds.feels: inferred: No inner life is legible here; they arrive as an impersonal, mechanical force, the sound of boots building and then the room exploding inward. They read as the enforcement of the trap rather than as individuals deciding anything.
minds.shows: Only their approach and their breach — 'the RUMBLE of combat BOOTS [.].'
minds.basis: The text presents them purely as an approaching sound and a physical incursion, with no dialogue, no reaction, no decision shown; there is nothing to read as an interior.

connects_back: Tank's 'It's a trap!' in sc-094, where he first recognised the setup — this scene is the trap springing on the isolated crew member.
The hardline being cut in sc-096 (bolt cutters through the main phone cable), which is exactly what Tank reports: 'They cut the hardline!'
The helicopter heard by Morpheus in sc-095, establishing the raid is already in the air as the crew moves — Mouse hears the same sound and is drawn toward it.
Morpheus's instruction in ev-021 to keep the Oracle's verdict secret, which has scattered and preoccupied the crew, leaving Mouse alone in Room 1313.
sets_up: Mouse being left behind / killed in the hotel raid (ev-022), since the room is now sealed and the intruders are inside with him.
The rest of the crew having to locate an extraction point and confirm Morpheus is alive without Mouse (ev-023), because the trap has removed one of them.
The Matrix's environment being mutable at the Agents' will — the bricked-up windows — which raises the stakes for every subsequent raid and escape (ev-023 through ev-027).
dramatic_function: It converts the abstract warning of a trap into an immediate, physical catastrophe, isolating and dooming Mouse to raise the cost of the Oracle's prophecy; it also establishes that the Matrix itself can be rewritten against the crew, so the environment is now a weapon as much as the Agents are.
